This study reads health and fitness summaries — such as steps, distance, heart rate, calories, and floors climbed — that your own apps and devices have already written to Health Connect.

Chronicle uses this only for the research study you enrolled in. Access is read-only: Chronicle never writes, changes, or deletes any data in Health Connect, and it never shares this data with anyone outside the study.

You choose whether to share each type of data, and you can change or revoke this access at any time in Health Connect or in the Chronicle Data Sharing screen.

Effective and last updated August 25, 2026.

Scope and responsibility. Chronicle is a reusable research data-collection app. The app publisher maintains the Android client. Each research study is separately responsible for its protocol, participant consent, server, retention rules, disclosures, contacts, and participant rights. A participant can have only one active Chronicle study on a device at a time.

Information Chronicle may handle. An enrolled study supplies a study identifier and participant reference. Chronicle creates a device-instance identifier and records consent choices. Depending on the modules the study requests and the participant accepts, this public release may collect app package names and usage timing; in-app activity class names; device lifecycle, battery, storage, thermal, connectivity, settings, and per-app network byte-count data; and participant category selections made after device unlock.

Information the public app does not collect. This public release does not collect audio or media-session data, Health Connect records, physical-activity or sleep data, accessibility events, notification content or notification metadata, precise location, hardware sensor measurements, contacts, messages, typed text, websites or search terms, screenshots, photos, videos, microphone recordings, advertising identifiers, financial information, or advertising profiles. It contains no advertising or cross-app tracking SDK.

Purpose and sharing. Information is used only to operate the enrolled research protocol, monitor collection and data quality, secure and troubleshoot the service, prevent unauthorized or duplicate requests, honor withdrawal and deletion, and meet the obligations stated by the study. Chronicle does not sell research data or use it for advertising, marketing, credit, insurance, or medical decisions. Data is sent only to the one public HTTPS server identified by the active study. That server may make data available to the responsible research institution, its authorized study team, and service providers permitted by the study notice or law.

Background operation and permissions. Accepted modules may collect and upload on a schedule while the app is closed. Usage Access is requested only for accepted app-usage modules. If unlock-based user identification is accepted, Android may show an ongoing foreground-service notification and an identification prompt after device unlock. Chronicle does not request Notification Listener, Accessibility, Activity Recognition, Health Connect, microphone, camera, or location access in this public release. Revoking an Android permission stops the affected source but does not itself send a study withdrawal request.

Storage, security, and retention. Pending research records and enrollment credentials are encrypted on the device. Records are sent over an authenticated encrypted connection to the active study server. Local queues remain until delivery, withdrawal, deletion, or a documented safety limit removes old pending records. Server retention is controlled by the study consent and approved protocol. No security measure can guarantee absolute protection.

Choices, withdrawal, and deletion. Participants can review module status in Data Sharing. Declining a module in Data Sharing stops its collection and deletes that module's pending on-device records before upload; a shared untagged queue may require deleting other pending records as the privacy-safe fallback. Turning off unlock identification in Settings instead stops future prompts and records an unassigned transition; already queued usage remains until delivery or withdrawal. To withdraw, open Chronicle Settings and choose Withdraw from study. Chronicle immediately stops local collection, sends an authenticated withdrawal request to the active study server, and clears local research data after the server request succeeds or after Chronicle records that the study team must be contacted to finish server-side deletion. Uninstalling stops the app but does not by itself notify the server; withdraw first or contact the study team.

Children and study eligibility. Chronicle is not a general consumer service for children. A minor may participate only under an approved study protocol with any required parent or guardian permission and participant assent.

Contact. Questions about participation, research records, retention, or rights should go to the research team named by the active study. Questions about the Chronicle Android application or publisher-level privacy inquiries may be sent to uzairalam998@gmail.com. Baylor College of Medicine general institutional privacy policy is available at https://www.bcm.edu/privacy.

These research records are encrypted on this device and uploaded to the enrolled study server shown during enrollment for the authorized research team. If you continue, Chronicle will show a prompt after device unlock asking whether the person using the device is the study participant or someone else. Chronicle records only the selection and when it was made, then uploads that record securely to the enrolled study server. You can turn this feature off later.
